releases.title: Say the Whole Paragraph
releases.summary: The chat box grows as you talk, the panel and card resize, Buddy can say his bubble lines out loud, and task sessions start on Opus 5.5.

lines: Talk as long as you like.
Pull my corners to resize me.

slides.title: Say the whole paragraph
slides.text: Dictate or type as much as you like: the chat box wraps and the panel grows upward with it (up to half the screen, then it scrolls). Enter sends; Shift-Enter starts a new line.

slides.title: Size them your way
slides.text: Drag any edge or corner of the chat panel to resize it, and the little grip in the usage card's corner to scale the whole card. Both remember their size and spot.

slides.title: Bubbles that talk
slides.text: Turn on Say my bubble lines out loud (right-click > Voice, or setup) and his quips come through the same voice as his answers. The Talk out loud slider still sets how many; he never talks over himself.

scene.line: Did I say that out loud?

slides.title: Pick the model
slides.text: Sessions Buddy starts for you run on Opus 5.5. Say "use Sonnet" (or Haiku, Fable, Opus) when you hand over a job, and the yes-or-no question shows which model it'll use.

scene.line: Start it on Sonnet? Yes or no.

new: The chat box now wraps and grows as you talk or type, and the panel grows with it so you can read the whole paragraph; Enter sends and it shrinks back.
Resize the chat panel from any edge or corner, and drag the usage card's bottom-right corner to make the whole card bigger or smaller; Buddy remembers both.
Buddy can now say his speech-bubble lines out loud: a new "Say my bubble lines out loud" switch in the Voice menu and setup, next to "Say my answers out loud".
Task sessions now start on Opus 5.5, and you can ask for another model when you hand Buddy a job, like "start a session with Sonnet".
better: Spoken chat answers that are lists are read out now (headings and code stay silent), and the console says why an answer stayed silent.
fixed: Buddy now stops making a spoken line as soon as it's replaced, so slow voice engines can't pile up and run the Mac out of memory.

releases.title: Every AI on One Card
releases.summary: The usage card can now show Codex, OpenRouter, xAI credits and your Grok plan alongside Claude, set up in the setup wizard.

lines: I can count all your AIs now.
Your keys stay in your Keychain.

slides.title: Every AI on one card
slides.text: Turn on the other AIs you use in the setup wizard and the card lists them under Claude, each with its tightest limit; click a row to see them all. Keys stay in your Keychain, and Buddy can tell you when one turns red.

scene.line: Codex is at 40%. Want the rest?

new: The usage card can show Codex, OpenRouter, xAI credits and your Grok plan alongside Claude; pick them in the setup wizard (two new steps). Nothing changes until you do.
API keys for the other AIs are stored in your macOS Keychain, and an optional red alert has Buddy speak up when any AI's limit turns red (off by default).

releases.title: Buddy Feels Alive
releases.summary: Smoother eyes, sleepy idle moves, a power-up hop when Claude finishes, a wobble when you carry him, and a soft glow during live voice chats.

slides.title: More alive
slides.text: Buddy's eyes glance smoothly at your mouse, he yawns and dozes off when you're away, hops with stars when a Claude Code session finishes, and wobbles and bounces when you carry him.

slides.title: He glows while he listens
slides.text: A soft halo surrounds Buddy for the whole live voice chat, in each skin's own colour. Skins can set their own with a glow colour in their JSON.

scene.line: I'm all ears. See the glow?

new: Buddy's eyes glance smoothly at your mouse, he yawns and dozes off when you're away, hops with stars when a Claude Code session finishes, and wobbles and bounces when you carry him.
Buddy glows softly while a live voice chat is on, in each skin's own colour (optional "glow" colour in a skin's JSON).

releases.title: Say Okay Buddy
releases.summary: Say "okay Buddy" and keep talking: he answers out loud. Plus personality dials, random skin changes and a list of your AI tools.

slides.title: Talk to me
slides.text: Say okay Buddy and just talk. He listens on your Mac and answers out loud, mouth in time; the Talk out loud slider sets how often he speaks his quips. Right-click > Voice > Listen (mic, macOS 26, Command Line Tools).

scene.line: You said okay Buddy? I'm listening.

slides.title: Just keep talking
slides.text: Say okay Buddy once and chat out loud. Talk over me whenever, and say we're done or stop listening when you're finished. I step aside while another app uses the mic. Switch: Right-click > Voice.

slides.title: Turn my dials
slides.text: Option-click Buddy to open setup and set humour, sarcasm, honesty, warmth and wordiness from 0 to 100, TARS style. They shape how he talks in chat, jobs and Telegram when a brain is set up.

slides.title: Skin shuffle
slides.text: Pick how often Buddy swaps costumes, every 1 to 24 hours, under Skin > Change on its own. He stays quiet about it during Quiet hours and never interrupts the Halloween costume.

new: Say "okay Buddy" and talk: Buddy listens on your Mac, answers out loud with his mouth in time, and can say his own quips out loud too (off until you turn it on under Right-click > Voice).
"Okay Buddy" now starts a live voice chat: keep talking with no wake word, talk over him any time, and say "we're done" to end it (Right-click > Voice > Keep listening).
TARS-style personality dials in setup: humour, sarcasm, honesty, warmth and wordiness, each 0 to 100.
Buddy can change into a random skin every few hours; turn it on under Skin > Change on its own.
Buddy can tell you which AI tools are on your Mac (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok, Kimi and more), which are open, and how recently each was used. Ask him in chat.
Buddy can see every Claude Code session on your Mac, summarise one, and type a message into it when you ask (tagged as from Buddy). Opt in with sessions = true in config.lua.
fixed: Buddy now speaks the whole of a long message instead of stopping after two sentences.

releases.title: Buddy on Your Phone
releases.summary: Telegram gets buttons, photos, voice notes and one-tap approvals. Buddy keeps notes, watches things, and takes lines from other programs.

slides.title: Buddy on your phone
slides.text: Send Buddy a photo and he looks at it. Ask for a voice reply and he sends a voice note. Answers type out live as he thinks, and the / menu lists what he can do. His profile says when the Mac is awake.

messages.text: That's a port clash: something else is on 3000. Want me to find it?

slides.title: One-tap approvals
slides.text: When a task session asks for permission, Buddy sends the request to Telegram with Allow once and Deny buttons. One tap answers it on the Mac. Each task can get its own topic in the chat.

messages.text:
Task "dark mode" wants to run: npm test
[ Allow once ]  [ Deny ]

slides.title: A better memory
slides.text: Buddy keeps what you tell him as short notes. /notes shows them, /forget 3 drops one, and he can look back through old chats when you ask about something from before.

scene.line: You told me Tuesday: standup moved to 9:30. Still true?

slides.title: Watches
slides.text: Ask Buddy to keep an eye on something. He checks on the interval you give and only speaks up when the answer changes.

messages.text: Watching every 30 min. I'll only message you when it changes.

slides.title: Other programs can hand Buddy a line
slides.text: Turn on notices in config.lua and any script on your Mac can drop a line in Buddy's inbox. He says it in the bubble, keeps it in the chat and sends it to Telegram when you're away.

scene.line: Lunch logged: 620 kcal. 2,480 to go today.

slides.title: A cleaner look
slides.text: The card, bubble, chat, setup wizard and this window now share one set of colours, spacing and type, so everything reads as one piece. The pixel buddy and his skins are untouched.

new: On Telegram, Buddy takes photos, sends voice notes, types answers out live, reacts to your messages and has a / command menu. All on once Telegram is paired.
Task sessions can ask for permission on Telegram: tap Allow once or Deny. Each task can get its own topic.
/notes shows what Buddy remembers about you and /forget drops one; he can search old chats when you ask about something from before.
/watch 30m <question> makes Buddy check on an interval and only speak up when the answer changes.
Other programs on your Mac can hand Buddy a line to say in the bubble, chat and Telegram (turn on with notices = true in config.lua).
better: The card, bubble, chat, setup, approval and What's New windows share one theme and read as one piece.
fixed: The chat and approval windows no longer sit in a gray box; their shadow fits the rounded panel.
On macOS 26 and later, the chart, setup and What's New windows no longer show the desktop through their title bars.

releases.title: Task Sessions
releases.summary: Hand Buddy a bigger job and he opens a Claude Code session for it that you can drive from your phone.

slides.title: Hand Buddy a bigger job
slides.text: Ask in the chat or on Telegram, or send /task and what it's for. After your yes, Buddy opens a Claude Code session just for that job in a new Terminal window.

scene.line: Start a Claude Code session for this? Reply yes or no.

slides.title: Drive it from your phone
slides.text: Every session has Remote Control on, and Buddy sends you its link. Its updates come to the chat, and to Telegram when you're away. Reply to one to answer it.

messages.text: /task add a dark mode to my app
Dark mode is up. Drive it from your phone: claude.ai/code/…
Dark mode: done! Should it be on by default?

new: Ask Buddy for a bigger job in the chat or on Telegram, or send /task, and after your yes he opens a Claude Code session for it with Remote Control on.
Buddy passes each session's updates on in the chat, and on Telegram when you're away. Reply to an update to answer that session (needs tmux: brew install tmux).
/tasks lists the sessions and /stop ends one. The right-click menu's Task sessions reopens a window, copies a link or stops one.

releases.title: The Halloween Update
releases.summary: Halloween week, a Buddy who learns alongside you, and new ways to make him your own.

slides.title: Halloween week
slides.text: Until October 31, Buddy's corner turns spooky: a witch hat, a candy pail, a spider on its web, bats, and a little skit every couple of minutes. It switches off by itself on November 1.

slides.title: A sidekick that learns
slides.text: With watching on, Buddy learns your apps, picks his own reactions and makes up lines about what you're doing. Health check-ins nudge you to move and eat. Option-click Buddy to choose what he watches.

scene.line: YouTube for the third time today.

slides.title: 63 skins
slides.text: Right-click Buddy and pick Skin. Try an outfit, a costume, or Surprise me. Your choice stays on after a restart.

slides.title: Click what Buddy says
slides.text: Click Buddy's speech bubble to open the chat on that line. You can pick up the conversation right where Buddy left off.

slides.title: Text Buddy from your phone
slides.text: Pair Telegram in the setup wizard, then ask Buddy about your usage while you're away. Your Mac needs to be awake to answer.

messages.text: Example: 42% of your weekly plan used.
Anytime. I've got my eye on it!

slides.title: What your Claude use is worth
slides.text: Click the API value row to pick a period, from this session to all time. See what your use would cost at API prices, how it compares with your plan, and a fun everyday comparison. These numbers are examples.

new: Halloween week: a spooky corner, a candy pail and 41 skits until October 31.
Buddy can learn your apps, make up lines on the spot and look after your health. Run the setup wizard again to choose what he watches.
Pick from 63 skins in Buddy's right-click menu.
Text Buddy from your phone after pairing Telegram in the setup wizard.
See a welcome tour and patch notes when Buddy updates.
better: Click Buddy's speech bubble to open the chat on what Buddy just said.
Pick a period for the card's API value row and see plan and everyday comparisons.
